([[Hazel Green, Alabama]]) | college = [[Alabama Crimson Tide men's basketball|Alabama]] (2018–2020) | highlights = * First-team All-[[Southeastern Conference|SEC]] (2020) * [[Southeastern Conference|SEC]] All-Freshman Team (2019) | medal_templates = {{MedalSport|Men's basketball}} {{MedalCountry|{{bk|USA}}}} {{MedalCompetition|[[FIBA Under-19 Basketball World Cup|FIBA Under-19 World Cup]]}} {{MedalGold|[[2019 FIBA Under-19 Basketball World Cup|2019 Greece]]|[[United States men's national under-19 basketball team|Team]]}} }} '''Kira Aundrea Lewis Jr.''' (born April 6, 2001) is an American [[basketball]] player. He played [[college basketball]] for the [[Alabama Crimson Tide men's basketball|Alabama Crimson Tide]]. ==High school career== [[File:Kira Lewis Jr (cropped).jpg|thumb|left|upright|Lewis at the [[Nike Elite Youth Basketball League|Nike EYBL]] in 2018]] Lewis played basketball for [[Hazel Green High School]] in [[Hazel Green, Alabama]] for three years. As a junior, he averaged 28.5 points, 5.9 rebounds, 4.5 assists, and 3.9 steals per game and led his team to the Alabama Class 6A semifinals. Lewis earned first-team All-State honors for his second consecutive season, was a finalist for [[Alabama Mr. Basketball]], and was named [[Huntsville, Alabama|Huntsville]] Region Player of the Year and Alabama Class 6A Player of the Year.{{cite web |last1=Boyette |first1=Daniel |title=Hazel Green's Kira Lewis stepped up as leader, earns Huntsville top basketball honor |url=https://www.al.com/highschoolsports/article/hazel-greens-kira-lewis-is-the-huntsville-region-boys-basketball-player-of-the-year/ |website=AL.com |accessdate=December 3, 2019 |date=March 20, 2018}} He was originally in the 2019 class but graduated early from high school and reclassified to 2018.{{cite web |title=Alabama Men’s Basketball Signs Kira Lewis, will Enroll in Classes this Fall |url=https://rolltide.com/news/2018/8/15/alabama-mens-basketball-signs-kira-lewis-will-enroll-in-classes-this-fall.aspx |publisher=University of Alabama Athletics |accessdate=December 3, 2019 |date=August 15, 2018}} On August 10, 2018, Lewis committed to [[Alabama Crimson Tide men's basketball|Alabama]] over several major [[NCAA Division I]] offers, including from [[Indiana Hoosiers men's basketball|Indiana]] and [[Kansas Jayhawks men's basketball|Kansas]]. He was considered a four-star [[college recruiting|recruit]] by [[ESPN]] and [[247Sports.com|247Sports]].{{cite web |last1=Daniels |first1=Evan |title=Kira Lewis commits to Alabama, reclassifies to 2018 |url=https://247sports.com/college/basketball/recruiting/Article/Kira-Lewis-commits-to-Alabama-reclassifies-to-2018-120549701/ |publisher=[[247Sports.com|247Sports]] |accessdate=December 3, 2019 |date=August 10, 2018}} ==College career== In his freshman season with Alabama, Lewis, at age 17, was the second-youngest player in NCAA Division I basketball behind Everett Perrot of [[Pepperdine Waves men's basketball|Pepperdine]] and was the youngest player to appear in a game. Lewis scored six points in his first career game versus [[Southern Jaguars men's basketball|Southern]]. The following game, he had 21 points against [[Appalachian State Mountaineers men's basketball|Appalachian State]] and followed that up with a season-high 24 points against [[Wichita State Shockers men's basketball|Wichita State]].{{cite web |last1=Walsh |first1=Christopher |title=The talk about Kira Lewis Jr. is shifting from his age to his consistency |url=https://www.si.com/college/alabama/bamacentral/the-talk-about-kira-lewis-jr-is-shifting-from-his-age-to-his-consistency-VlPcBLHfAkeYII-cLqCZAQ/ |website=[[Sports Illustrated]] |accessdate=December 3, 2019 |date=January 22, 2019}} He tied his season-high of 24 points against [[Georgia Bulldogs men's basketball|Georgia]] in February 2019.{{cite news |last1=Casagrande |first1=Michael |title=Kira Lewis is staying at Alabama after flirting with transfer |url=https://www.al.com/alabamabasketball/2019/04/kira-lewis-is-staying-at-alabama-after-flirting-with-transfer.html |accessdate=December 10, 2019 |work=Al.com |date=April 8, 2019}} Lewis averaged 13.5 points, 2.9 assists, and 2.6 rebounds per game and was named to the [[Southeastern Conference|SEC]] All-Freshman Team. However, Alabama struggled and finished 18–16, losing in the first round of the NIT. Lewis entered the transfer portal before new coach [[Nate Oats]] convinced him to return.{{cite news |last1=Martin |first1=Tyler |title=Alabama Will Look to an Older, More Experienced Kira Lewis Jr. for Success Under Nate Oats |url=https://www.si.com/college/alabama/bamacentral/alabama-basketball-kira-lewis-jr-nate-oats/ |accessdate=December 10, 2019 |work=[[Sports Illustrated]] |date=October 25, 2019}} In his sophomore season opener, Lewis scored a then-career-high 30 points in an 81–80 loss to [[Penn Quakers men's basketball|Penn]].{{cite news |title=Dingle lifts Penn to 81–80 opening win over Alabama |url=https://www.espn.com/mens-college-basketball/recap?gameId=401169798 |accessdate=December 10, 2019 |work=[[ESPN]] |agency=[[Associated Press]] |date=November 5, 2019}} Lewis scored a career-high 37 points on February 8, 2020, in a 105–102 overtime win against [[Georgia Bulldogs men's basketball|Georgia]].{{cite news |title=Lewis scores career-high 37 as Alabama tops Georgia in OT |url=https://www.espn.com/mens-college-basketball/recap?gameId=401166337 |accessdate=August 24, 2020 |work=[[ESPN]] |agency=[[Associated Press]] |date=February 8, 2020}} On February 12, he became the first Alabama player since 1996 to record a triple double, posting 10 points, 10 rebounds and 13 assists in a 95–91 overtime loss to [[Auburn Tigers men's basketball|Auburn]]. He became the 2nd player in school history to reach this accomplishment.{{cite news |title=Wiley, No. 11 Auburn survive in OT again, 95–91 over Alabama |url=https://www.espn.com/mens-college-basketball/recap?gameId=401166344 |accessdate=August 24, 2020 |work=[[ESPN]] |agency=[[Associated Press]] |date=February 12, 2020}} On February 25, Lewis contributed 29 points, seven rebounds, and four assists in a 80–73 loss to [[Mississippi State Bulldogs men's basketball|Mississippi State]].{{cite news |last1=Stephens |first1=Hannah |title=Alabama loses game, John Petty against Miss State |url=https://rolltidewire.usatoday.com/2020/02/25/alabama-loses-game-john-petty-against-miss-state/ |accessdate=February 27, 2020 |work=Roll Tide Wire |date=February 25, 2020}} At the conclusion of the regular season, Lewis was named to the First Team All-SEC.{{cite press release|url=https://www.secsports.com/article/28877731/sec-announces-2020-men-basketball-awards |title=SEC announces 2020 Men's Basketball Awards |publisher=Southeastern Conference |date=March 10, 2020 |accessdate=March 10, 2020}} As a sophomore, Lewis averaged 18.5 points, 4.8 rebounds, and 5.2 assists per game.{{cite web |last1=Tsoukalas |first1=Tony |title=How to watch: Alabama basketball vs Tennessee in the SEC Tournament |url=https://alabama.rivals.com/news/how-to-watch-alabama-basketball-vs-tennessee-in-the-sec-tournament |website=Rivals.com |accessdate=March 22, 2020}} After the season, Lewis declared for the [[2020 NBA draft]].{{cite web |last1=Potter |first1=Charlie |title=Alabama's Kira Lewis, John Petty to test NBA draft waters |url=https://247sports.com/college/alabama/Article/Alabama-Basketball-Kira-Lewis-John-Petty-to-test-NBA-draft-waters-145346895/ |website=247 Sports |date=March 24, 2020|accessdate=March 25, 2020}} ==National team career== Lewis played for the [[United States men's national under-19 basketball team|United States]] at the [[2019 FIBA Under-19 Basketball World Cup|2019 FIBA Under-19 World Cup]] in [[Heraklion]], Greece. He averaged four points and 1.6 assists per game and helped his team win a gold medal.{{cite web |last1=Villicana |first1=Paloma |title=Kira Lewis brings back gold to north Alabama |url=https://www.waff.com/2019/07/09/kira-lewis-brings-back-gold-north-alabama/ |publisher=[[WAFF (TV)|WAFF]] |accessdate=December 3, 2019 |date=July 8, 2019}} ==Career statistics== {{NBA player statistics legend}} ===College=== {{NBA player statistics start}} |- | style="text-align:left;"| [[2018–19 NCAA Division I men's basketball season|2018–19]] | style="text-align:left;"| [[2018–19 Alabama Crimson Tide men's basketball team|Alabama]] | '''34''' || '''34''' || 31.6 || .433 || .358 || .783 || 2.6 || 2.9 || .8 || .3 || 13.5 |- | style="text-align:left;"| [[2019–20 NCAA Division I men's basketball season|2019–20]] | style="text-align:left;"| [[2019–20 Alabama Crimson Tide men's basketball team|Alabama]] | 31 || 31 || '''37.6''' || '''.459''' || '''.366''' || '''.802''' || '''4.8''' || '''5.2''' || '''1.8''' || '''.6''' || '''18.5''' |- class="sortbottom" | style="text-align:center;" colspan="2"| Career | 65 || 65 || 34.5 || .447 || .362 || .793 || 3.6 || 4.0 || 1.3 || .4 || 15.9 {{S-end}} ==References== {{Reflist}} ==External links== *[https://rolltide.com/sports/mens-basketball/roster/kira-lewis-jr-/5693 Alabama Crimson Tide bio] *[https://www.usab.com/basketball/players/mens/l/lewis-kira.aspx USA Basketball bio] {{DEFAULTSORT:Lewis, Kira Jr.}} [[Category:2001 births]] [[Category:Living people]] [[Category:Alabama Crimson Tide men's basketball players]] [[Category:American men's basketball players]] [[Category:Basketball players from Alabama]] [[Category:People from Madison County, Alabama]] [[Category:Point guards]]
